# Sirach Chapter 13 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_013_page_001.jpg

---

**13:1** Whoever touches pitch will be defiled, and whoever associates with an arrogant person will become like him.

**13:2** Do not take up a burden beyond your strength, and do not associate with someone mightier and wealthier than yourself. What does a clay pot have in common with an iron kettle? The kettle strikes and the pot is shattered.

**13:3** A rich man wrongs someone and adds insults; a poor man is wronged and must himself offer apologies.

**13:4** If you can be of use, he will exploit you; but if you are no longer useful, he will abandon you.

**13:5** If you possess anything, he will live with you; he will empty you out and not feel sorry.

**13:6** Does he need you? He will deceive you; he will smile at you and raise your hopes; he will speak pleasantly to you and ask, "What do you need?"

**13:7** He will put you to shame at his banquets, and this more than once or twice, until he has stripped you bare; and in the end he will mock you. Afterward when he sees you, he will pass by you and shake his head at you.

**13:8** Guard yourself from being misled and from being humiliated by your own entertainment.

**13:9** When an important man invites you, hold back; and the more he will press you.

**13:10** Do not push forward, lest you be thrust back; do not stay too far back, lest you be forgotten.

**13:11** Do not presume to speak as his equal, and do not trust his lengthy speeches; for by much talking he will test you, and with a smile he will probe you.

**13:12** One who shows no mercy is one who does not control his words; he will not spare you hurt or chains.

**13:13** Be on guard and be very careful, for you are walking with your own downfall. When you hear these things, wake up in your sleep.

**13:14** Love the Lord all your life, and call upon him for your salvation.

**13:15** Every creature loves its own kind, and every person loves his neighbor.

**13:16** All flesh keeps to its own kind, and people associate with those like themselves.

**13:17** What fellowship does a wolf have with a lamb? No more does a sinner have with a righteous person.

**13:18** What peace is there between a hyena and a dog? And what peace between a rich man and a poor man?

**13:19** Wild asses in the wilderness are the prey of lions; so too, poor people are the feeding ground of the rich.

**13:20** Humility is an abomination to the proud; so too, a poor man is an abomination to the rich.

**13:21** When a rich person stumbles, he is upheld by friends; but when a poor person falls, his friends as well push him away.

**13:22** When a rich man slips, many rush to help; he says something improper and they excuse him. When a poor man slips, they rebuke him on top of it; he speaks sensibly and no one takes notice.

**13:23** The rich man speaks and everyone is quiet, and they praise his words to the sky; the poor man speaks and they ask, "Who is this?" And if he stumbles, they push him further down.

**13:24** Wealth is good where there is no sin attached to it; poverty is evil in the opinion of the ungodly.

**13:25** A man's heart changes his expression, whether for good or for evil.

**13:26** A glad countenance is a sign of a glad heart; but devising wise sayings involves wearisome effort.
